title: What a Guest Owes on a Settled Loss under the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan
content:
Where a loss on a trip is settled against the guest, what the guest owes under the Keyturn Guest Protection
Plan is the deductible of the level in force on the day of the loss, capped by that level's responsibility
ceiling for the kind of damage, and the ceiling governs wherever it is the lower of the two.

A level whose deductible is nil charges nothing whatever the loss, and a level that carries a responsibility
ceiling of nil leaves the guest owing nothing even where the host's own claim is met in full.

Where the level allows the deductible to be bought out, a guest who paid the buy-out fee before the trip started
owes nothing on the loss, and the buy-out is not sold once the trip has started.

A deductible may be paid over the level's instalments, spaced by the level's instalment interval, counted in
whole calendar days from the day the previous instalment fell due; each instalment is posted as its own line so
that the instalments stay separable.

The guest also bears the level's share of the host's loss of use and of the appraisal cost, each posted as its
own line with its own basis rather than folded into the deductible.

A deductible already raised is written off where the finding of fault changes, where the loss is later refused,
or where the level was misapplied, and the write-off names the line it clears.

The guest may dispute a deductible inside the level's dispute window, counted in whole calendar days from the
day the deductible was raised, and a dispute lodged inside the window stops recovery until it is decided.

## The two figures and which of them governs

The deductible of the level in force on the day of the loss and that level's responsibility ceiling for the kind
of damage are both read, and the lower of the two is what the guest owes. Where the level's deductible is nil,
nothing is owed whatever the loss; where the ceiling for that kind of damage is nil, nothing is owed even where
the host's own claim is met in full.

## The dispute window read as a clock

The clock starts on the day the deductible was raised, which is the date standing on the protection line
correlated by its own reference number, and it is read before the deductible is written off. The window is the
level's own, counted in whole calendar days, and the last day of the window is inside it. On a hypothetical
window of 14 calendar days beginning with a deductible raised on the tenth of a month, a dispute lodged on the
twenty-third day of that month is on the fourteenth day counted from the day it was raised and is inside the
window; lodged on the twenty-fourth it is outside it.

## Separately posted lines

| What is posted | On what basis |
|---|---|
| Each instalment of a deductible | Its own line, so that the instalments stay separable |
| The guest's share of the host's loss of use | Its own line, on its own basis |
| The guest's share of the appraisal cost | Its own line, on its own basis |
| A write-off of a deductible already raised | Names the line it clears |
